prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Electrical Technology for solving simple DC and AC circuits.
Basic notions of Differential and Integral Calculus
Basic notions of Waves and Electromagnetism
Basic notions of Fundamentals of Informatics

learning_outcomes.text: Possess a general overview of electronics in its different branches and fields of application.
Know the behavior, characteristics, and main applications of electronic devices.
Analyze and understand the operation of circuits containing electronic components.
Handle datasheets of integrated circuits for analog or digital applications and use some of them in basic assemblies.
Handle laboratory electronic instrumentation and equipment and perform static and temporal measurements.

syllabus_topics: Analog integrated circuits. The ideal operational amplifier.
Fundamentals of digital design. Boolean algebra.
Laboratory Practice 1. Laboratory safety. Handling laboratory equipment I.
Laboratory Practice 2. Handling laboratory equipment II.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and laboratory components. The final theoretical grade for students with 80% or more attendance is the average of EP-I and EP-II, provided each partial has 4 or more points; otherwise, the maximum theoretical grade is 4.5. For students with less than 80% attendance, the average of EP-I and EP-II must each be 5 or more points; otherwise, the maximum theoretical grade is 4.5. The final course grade is calculated as (0.80 × Theory) + (0.20 × Laboratory), if minimum requirements are met. Otherwise, the final grade is the lesser of the calculated grade and 4.5. For the extraordinary call, students must achieve a minimum of 5 out of 10 in each component (theory and laboratory) to pass, with the final grade calculated using the same formula.
